title: An unusual case of vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis.
ehr_evidence: The data source was a single-patient clinical case presentation with diagnostic workup (MRI, electromyography, cerebrospinal fluid analysis, stool cultures, and polio serology), not electronic or computerised individual-level health records.
summary: A case report of an immunocompetent, previously well child nearly one year of age who developed vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis after receiving oral poliovirus vaccine despite two prior doses of inactivated poliovirus vaccine.
key_findings: The child was determined to be a probable case of vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis (VAPP) by the Advisory Committee Causality Assessment.
Stool culture isolated poliovirus type 3, sequenced at the national laboratory in China as a Sabin poliovirus type 3 strain with 99.7% homology with the parent OPV strain.
Repeat polio serology seven months after the first set showed a 1:8 titre for poliovirus 3.
Estimates of risk for VAPP range from one in 750,000 with the first dose of OPV to one in 2.4 million for all doses of OPV.
captured_features: MRI findings of bilateral symmetric increased signal within the anterior horns of the spinal cord gray matter (C2-C5 and T10-T12)
Electromyography showing denervation, absent peroneal nerve response, and fibrillation potentials
Cerebrospinal fluid white blood cell count of 12×106/L with protein 1.43 g/L
Stool culture results (poliovirus type 3, no nonpolio enteroviral growth)
Polio antibody titres (1:8 for poliovirus 1, 1:32 for poliovirus 2, 1:128 for poliovirus 3)
Immunoglobulin subclass analysis and negative HIV test
population: A previously well child almost one year of age, born in Canada to Chinese parents, evaluated in China and Canada
limitations: Single case report of one patient, limiting generalizability and causal inference
Retrospective case review without a control group
